subject: Post-call: Deployment path & identity/KMS/log retention clarifications
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Jacobs <sara.jacobs@nexahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-06T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Deployment path & identity/KMS/log retention clarifications

Hi Sara — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have alignment.

Call highlights (TL;DR)
- Primary driver: regulatory audit for PHI workflows and long-term evidence retention.
- Identity: Okta SAML + SCIM provisioning for users and groups.
- Key management: customer must use an HSM-backed KMS (BYOK preferred).
- Logging: immutable retention requirement in your audit — target 6+ years; tamper-evident storage is important.
- Networking: you mentioned a private peering/VPC connector requirement and potential on-prem gateway in some sites.

How the deployment modes map to these asks (high-level)
- Hosted API: best for time-to-value but cannot provide customer-controlled HSM or guaranteed immutable 6+ year logs in a customer-controlled store.
- Dedicated capacity: can meet stronger isolation and we can integrate cloud HSMs (subject to CSP limits) and export streams to your log retention service — may need a sidecar for BYOK wrapping in some cloud setups.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full control for BYOK + HSM and long-term immutable logs in your environment — this is the most likely fit if BYOK + 6-year immutable retention are hard requirements.

Requested next steps
1) Please confirm the exact Okta metadata endpoints (SAML issuer / SCIM base URL).
2) Confirm which CSP(s) you prefer for Dedicated (AWS, GCP, Azure) and whether you require CloudHSM or on-prem HSM.
3) Share an example retention policy or regulation clause that drives the 6+ year requirement.
4) We propose a technical deep-dive with our Solutions Engineering next week (30–45 min) to walk through the integration patterns and collection of evidence. Proposed slot: Tue 2026-10-12 10:00 PT.

Attached: redwood-deploy-options.pdf (deployment mapping), security-evidence-overview.pdf (SOC2 / logging examples).

If Dedicated or Private are likely, we will loop in Solutions Engineering and Legal early to scope procurement and entitlements. Happy to adjust based on your answers.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Sara Jacobs <sara.jacobs@nexahealth.com>

Cc: NexaHealth SRE <sre@nexahealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Deployment path & identity/KMS/log retention clarifications

Evelyn — appreciated the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Identity: Confirmed — Okta SAML for SSO (IdP initiated + SP redirect). SCIM required for provisioning; we can provide the SCIM token and base URL once we lock the cadence.
- KMS/HSM: We require HSM-backed key material and prefer BYOK. We operate across AWS and Azure; our security team prefers FIPS 140-2 Level 3 HSM for persistent key material if possible. If Dedicated can integrate with a CloudHSM or Azure Dedicated HSM and leave keys under our control, that might be acceptable.
- Logs: Our compliance team asked for 6 years of immutable retention for audit evidence. We use an S3-like immutable bucket (object lock) today and would need the ability to export/search logs into our archive.
- Networking/Residency: Data plane must stay in us-west-2 for a subset of workloads. We have one site requiring air-gapped export capability for a small dataset.

We are leaning towards Private but need numbers (approx cost and timeline) for Dedicated vs Private to present to procurement.

If you can confirm whether Hosted is off the table for BYOK and immutable 6-year logs, that will help. The proposed Tue slot works for me if you can confirm.

Thanks — Sara
Sara Jacobs
Director, Platform Security — NexaHealth
sara.jacobs@nexahealth.com

Date: 2026-10-07T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Deployment path & identity/KMS/log retention clarifications

Sara — thanks, and great details. I’ll summarize practical options and ask a few clarifying questions so SE can prepare for the deep-dive.

Quick mapping: 
- Hosted API: cannot satisfy BYOK/HSM or fully customer-controlled immutable 6-year archives. Hosted customers can stream logs to external sinks but the initial retention and custody remain cross-tenant and not suitable for your compliance ask.
- Dedicated: can be configured with stronger isolation; in AWS we can route key ops to a customer-controlled CloudHSM (requires cloud account linkage or a KMS proxy pattern). Azure Dedicated HSM is also an option. For strong BYOK guarantees, Dedicated often needs an integration pattern (sidecar or KMS proxy) that we’ll detail in the deep-dive.
- Private VPC / on-prem: supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and direct control of immutable storage — the default choice when auditors require internal custody.

Questions for your team (please reply inline if possible):
1) Which CSP(s) specifically? (you mentioned AWS + Azure). For Dedicated cost estimates we need to know which region(s) to size (e.g., us-west-2).
2) Does NexaHealth require hardware HSM (FIPS 140-2 Level 3) onsite, or is cloud HSM (AWS CloudHSM / Azure Dedicated HSM) acceptable?
3) Exact retention requirement: 6 years in immutable store — is there a regulatory citation or internal retention policy doc we can review?
4) Expected QPS / peak tokens per second for the production workload (rough order of magnitude).
5) Any hard procurement timeline / go-live date?
6) Compliance contacts we can loop in for evidence exchange (SOC2/ISO).

Proposed next steps
- Confirm answers above.
- Tech deep-dive Tue 2026-10-12 10:00 PT (30–45m). We’ll have Solutions Engineering + a Platform Architect on the call to diagram KMS options and log export patterns.
- If Private looks required after the call, we’ll prepare a preliminary scope and cost estimate for Legal and Procurement.

Attaching a short mapping sheet (deployment-triggers-mapping.xlsx) so we can capture responses.

Marissa Cole
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

All — quick note from a product/ops perspective. Thanks for driving the details, team.

Operational considerations
- If NexaHealth requires FIPS 140-2 Level 3 HSM with BYOK and immutable 6-year retention under customer control, our Private VPC or on-prem offering is the safe path. Dedicated can work if the customer accepts a cloud HSM model and the keys remain under their account or in a KMS proxy pattern; both approaches add engineering and procurement work.
- Estimated timeline: Dedicated (with cloud-HSM integration) ~8–10 weeks to provision + validate with SE and Security. Private on-prem/VPC (depending on network and air-gap needs) ~12–16+ weeks. We will give a granular SOW after the deep-dive.
- Commercial: Priya, please prepare a preliminary cost delta for Dedicated vs Private (ballpark). I’m authorizing a solutions-engagement budget for an initial PoC if the customer signs an MOU.

Next actions
1) Marissa: open the HubSpot opportunity (I’ve put a note with DEAL-8371). Add Rishi and Priya as followers.
